summary: St. Louis-born conservative activist Phyllis Schlafly, a secret John Birch Society member, used propaganda and a housewife lobbying network to defeat the Equal Rights Amendment and turn anti-feminism, anti-gay politics and abortion into lasting Republican culture wars.

evidence.note: birth in St. Louis; year garbled in transcript, 1924 from known record
first run for Congress and upset primary win, start of her political career
death at 92 shortly after endorsing Trump at a St. Louis rally
partnership with Admiral Chester Ward pushing nuclear superiority and first-strike capability
letters show she was a secret John Birch Society member from 1959
leads 1960 convention revolt against an anti-segregation platform plank
Birch Society bulk-bought and distributed her Goldwater book via a front publisher
founds STOP ERA and organizes housewives against the amendment
anti-gay campaigning, opposition to AIDS education in the 1980s
1996 deal with Buchanan to lock a no-exceptions abortion plank into the GOP platform
legacy traced to abortion polling and opinion shifts up to release

notes: Main span starts at her 1952 congressional run (year from known record; transcript gives no year). No theme for anti-LGBTQ politics, which gets a real segment; folded into religious-right-culture-war. weapons-arms-trade covers her nuclear-strategy books with Chester Ward. Eagle Forum stands in for STOP ERA and her newsletter network.
